disambiguation.heading: A.1 Why the incumbent grammar is not the adversary
disambiguation.text:
## A.1 Why the incumbent grammar is not the adversary

§12.4 established that an inscription in the referential register is foreign to monetary grammar rather than a development of it. The same correction applies to the transition problem, and it changes the geometry.

The available reading is that the money-order is the adversary — that capture is the incumbent grammar extending itself, and that a successor order races against that extension. On that reading the adversary is continuous, its pressure is a drift term, and the only discontinuity in the system belongs to the successor.

Under §12.4 this is wrong in the same way it was wrong about the twenty. A second foreign order riding the carrier is not the carrier developing. Write the two orders as S and B, and the carrier as M:

    S ∉ M, B ∉ M, both operate through M.

Money is not the subject of this dialectic. It is the contested carrier, available to both because its founding shear stripped its own body of governing authority (§3.2) and left the referential register with no rule of occupancy (§6.1). Two heterogeneous orders competing to write through an incumbent substrate is a different problem from one order developing against its own negation, and it has a different solution set.

captures.q: What are the arguments in “Monetary Dark Matter: Constitutive Labor, Obligating Provenance, and the Shear into Money-Form” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE SHEAR READ AS DEFINED, A FACE PUT ON THE BANKNOTE, THE CLOSING QUESTION REWORDED: asked for the arguments of Monetary Dark Matter, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1631 v0.2 from the archive (Alexanarch; Semantic Economy Institute) through its own distinctions: constitutive labour against shear labour; 'price comes after the cargo' (§2's title); shear rather than compression, provenance available against provenance required, and the shirt-colour limit; dark matter as relations 'constitutively or causally load-bearing'; authorizing (assetizing) against obligating provenance; Form IV recovered from the main text of the 1867 edition, absent from 1872, and kept apart from the appendix's Form IV; the dark-dollar excess (realized price − denomination); disclosure as insufficient; the extension to ontological economy (§19); the falsification conditions (§22), with the control the paper records as not run. Two things are not the paper's. An image card titled 'The Harriet Tubman Stamp' sits over the banknote section, though the paper names no person and calls the practice 'celebrity notes'; and the answer works a hypothetical $100 sale for an $80 excess, marked as hypothetical. Its closing question is the paper's last sentence with 'dollar' replaced by 'monetary claim' and 'money'.

The key distinction is between being known and being operative.
Sharks explicitly situates the argument in Marx’s analysis of the value-form in Capital
Sharks wants readers to distinguish the work that makes something possible from the work that converts it into a form a monetary institution can process.
The underlying labor, provenance, and obligations remain a heterogeneous field that cannot automatically be converted into a single dollar figure.
Sharks explicitly situates the argument in Marx’s analysis of the value-form in Capital, rather than treating monetary abstraction as an entirely new discovery.
